tools.name: export_video
tools.description: Render the timeline (or a range of it) to a video or audio file. Pick a `preset` (see `docs` topic `export`: "YouTube 1080p", "ProRes 422 HQ master", "ProRes 4444 with alpha", "DNxHR HQ master", "Web VP9", "Audio WAV 24-bit", …), or a `format` (mp4, mov, mkv, webm, m4a, wav, flac; default: the extension of `out`) with optional codec fields. HEVC and AV1 need a hardware encoder. Refused while placeholders are pending or media is offline, and for combinations that cannot be written (the error names the fields). Exports run one at a time in a queue shared with the app; the call returns a job id (use `job_status`, `cancel_job`), or the result with `wait`. `audioOnly` writes the mix alone; `loudness` normalises it to a target with a true-peak limit and the result reports loudness before and after. The result names the encoder used.

Later items ripple on sync-locked tracks, linked items edit together, times snap to the frame grid. `request` is the edit as JSON, e.g. {"op":"rippleDelete","tracks":["a1"],"ranges":[{"start":12.3,"end":14}]} (seconds). Returns the plan and the printed lines of what changed; a refusal names a code and the culprit item ids. With `rev`, a request made against an older revision is moved through the ripples made since.

Ids read at an older `rev` stay valid. `apply: false` returns the plan and the `timeline.tsx` diff without changing anything.
